title: Three-dimensional geometric estimation of preoperative soft-tissue volume in mucogingival surgery: A proof-of-concept case series
html:
Objective

This proof-of-concept study evaluated a digital workflow incorporating intraoperative scanning to provide additional geometric information on the treated area.

Methods

Five patients with gingival recessions underwent mucogingival surgery at 14 sites; eight received a subepithelial connective tissue graft and six were treated without grafting. Intraoral scans were obtained at baseline (BL), after periosteal exposure (PE), after graft placement (GP), when applicable, and at 1 month (1 M) and 3 months (3 M). Serial models were superimposed to calculate root mean square (RMS), surface-deviation metrics, and regional deviation scores. The PE model served as a geometric reference for Boolean reconstruction of external and internal volumetric components, while PE and GP scans were used to reconstruct initial graft volume.

Results

Digital measurements showed high intra-examiner reproducibility. Among three patients with complete longitudinal volumetric data, median external volume was 151.54 mm³ at BL, 270.67 mm³ at 1 M, and 240.19 mm³ at 3 M. External volume was numerically higher at 1 M and lower at 3 M, although pairwise comparisons were not significant after adjustment. Internal volume showed no significant overall difference across time points. RMS and related surface-deviation metrics did not differ significantly between BL–1 M and BL–3 M. Initial graft volume was reconstructed in three cases, ranging from 78.28 to 134.74 mm³.

Conclusions

The workflow integrated surface-deviation analysis with reconstruction of external and internal volumetric components and initial graft volume. These findings support the feasibility of incorporating intraoperative scans into three-dimensional assessment of mucogingival surgery, although validation in larger, standardized samples is required.

Clinical Significance

Intraoperative scanning combined with three-dimensional reconstruction may provide a feasible approach for estimating preoperative soft-tissue volume and assessing spatial changes after mucogingival surgery. This workflow may complement conventional clinical measurements in longitudinal soft-tissue assessment.
